justification: This changes how the free upzoning tool frames its regulatory eligibility result to the public. No logic, data, or query changes — but it alters user-facing planning communication on a compliance surface, so the wording must stay defensible: lead with what the mapped standards permit, phrase clearances as clearances, and keep the subject-to-a-DA caveat present exactly once rather than removed.

pre_impl.existing_data: The tool already returns per-form eligibility with source clauses and a green tick, but every status chip read as absence (not mapped here) and every eligible reason repeated the subject-to-a-DA parenthetical, so a confident cited result read as a hedge.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Verified live on 38 Park Road Bowral that duplex and secondary dwelling both return eligible with cited clauses, yet the surrounding copy undersold them; the fix is presentation only, the underlying eligibility is unchanged.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Copy-only edit to the existing page; reuses the same result object, formLabel helper and CheckCircle2 icon; no new component, engine call, or data source is introduced.

break_it.scenario: A lot returns no eligible forms at all so the new lead-in summary would have nothing to name
break_it.what_happens: an empty summary banner would render a bare or broken sentence claiming buildability where there is none
break_it.how: the summary block renders only when eligibleForms.length is greater than zero, so a no-eligible-forms result skips it and falls through to the per-form list
break_it.repro: run the tool on a non-residential or fully ineligible lot and confirm no green summary banner appears

break_it.scenario: The stripped subject-to-a-DA caveat disappears entirely, leaving the result reading as an approval rather than a screen
break_it.what_happens: removing the caveat everywhere would overstate the result as a decision instead of an indicative mapped-standards check
break_it.how: the parenthetical is stripped only from the eligible per-row reason; the section note above the list and the new summary line both still state with consent through a development application
break_it.repro: inspect an eligible card and confirm the caveat is absent inline but present in the section note and summary

break_it.scenario: A clearance chip such as heritage or dual-occupancy prohibition is mislabelled so a real constraint reads as clear
break_it.what_happens: a genuinely heritage-listed or dual-occ-prohibited lot shown as clear would understate a real planning constraint
break_it.how: the chips branch on the same boolean gates as before; only the false-branch wording changed from not mapped to an explicit no-constraint clearance, and the true branch still shows the constraint
break_it.repro: run a heritage-listed lot and confirm the chip reads Heritage listed, not No heritage listing

post_merge.manual_verify: tsc clean and the frontend jest suite passes; copy change verified against the live Bowral result which returns duplex and secondary dwelling eligible with cited clauses. Note surfaced separately: the tool 404s on the apex plotdetect.com.au (info-site project) and is only reachable on canibuildit.com.au and verify.plotdetect.com.au — a domain-placement task, not part of this copy change.
